audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted their own why-text and the packet. Level 1 was Irelia while whys[0] says 'it's even'; levels 4-5 and First item were Skill while whys[3] says 'survival, not trading, is the goal' and whys[5] says her Trinity Force spike 'keeps her ahead'; and 2+ items was Irelia while whys[6] and late both say Kayle out-scales her outright.
audit.why: At level 1 Irelia has no Bladesurge reset chain and Kayle has no transform. From 2 to first item her stun-into-reset all-in beats a Kayle with no dash. By 16 Kayle's fully ranged AoE autos and percent-HP E beat a finite duelist.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 5 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group — the same four rows the Irelia-side audit flipped — with ratings inverted to match and all four phases[].why lines rewritten.
sources: brief currentText whys[0], whys[3], whys[5], whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet counts one sequencing cue on the whole page. Flawless Duet is named as the tracked cooldown eleven times without a number, and the first-item phase gave no reason the spike is contested.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 — a 16s window at rank 1 is the only safe farming stretch Kayle gets pre-6. Her first item does not out-spike Irelia's Trinity Force timing, which is why that row is Irelia's.
audit.corrected: 16s written into dosFull[0].d and report[5].t; the first-item phase now states what actually happens instead of telling the reader to force a fight they lose.

audit.whatIsWrong: The anti-heal line said only 'his healing fights your pattern' and never said what heals. Bladesurge heals Irelia on every dash and its cooldown refreshes on a Marked target or a kill, which is the reason chip damage does not stick.
audit.why: Grievous Wounds timing is the entire counter to a Q-reset chain through the wave; naming the source makes the item purchase concrete.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now names Bladesurge as the heal, and report[5].t states the stun-into-reset chain that Flawless Duet enables.
sources: enemyKit Q text and heal flag

edits.before: You are the weakest level 1 in the game — pay rent quietly. Identify how Irelia contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — she has no Bladesurge reset chain yet and you have no transform, so take safe CS and give no early lead.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Flawless Duet's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: You lose every extended fight: Defiant Dance eats your burst and Bladesurge resets off the wave to stick to you — survive, do not trade.

edits.before: Nashor's Tooth is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Flawless Duet's cooldown.
edits.after: Nashor's narrows the gap, but her Trinity Force spike still edges the duel — poke, do not commit.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Irelia carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Fully ranged AoE autos she cannot dash out of, plus percent-HP E — kite her engages and melt her from range.

edits.before: Her engage CC. Survive it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 — step up only when it is down.

edits.before: Track Irelia's Flawless Duet (Stun): Her engage CC. Survive it. When it is down — E-poke + scale.
edits.after: Track Flawless Duet (16s): her stun into a Bladesurge reset. When it is down — E-poke and scale.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Nashor's Tooth  (the ramp begins), then Riftmaker / Rabadon's Deathcap; boots Sorcerer's Shoes. Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Nashor's Tooth (the ramp begins), then Riftmaker / Rabadon's Deathcap; boots Sorcerer's Shoes. Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — Bladesurge heals her on every dash.
